title: Assistant Agent + Overlay
observations: Two-phase review gate caught 3 integration wiring gaps (B1: SettingsAssistant unmounted, B2: pinning trigger, B3: tool-call schema). All components correct in isolation; integration gaps emerged only in code review. Builder fixed all 3 in 1h rework. Pattern: component-level correctness != container-assembly correctness.

Architecture plan reconciliation table (20 spec-vs-reality checks) prevented silent bugs and clarified assumptions (soulPrompt column exists, ThreadMessageAppendedEvent exists, PlainPayload shape confirmed). Atomized facts with line numbers saved 1-2h of investigation and potential wrong implementations.

Design-it-twice decisions (event-driven dispatcher vs inline dispatch, PlainPayload extension vs separate table) were genuine trade-off analysis grounded in architecture principles (layer boundaries, query cost). Both decisions held up in code review with no regrets.

TDD red phase (1751 LOC across 10 test files) provided comprehensive coverage before implementation. High-risk work (dispatcher, new tools, schema extensions) justified extensive test suite. All tests green on first build, prevented rework loop.

Design spec compliance gap: SettingsAssistant styling (font sizes, colors, capitalization) deviated from approved design contract. Non-blocking in code review but signals missed design-handoff verification. Small visual quality issue, not a functional defect.

Integration wiring gaps are systematic (3rd consecutive: AD7 contract violations, AE4 drawer animation, AD8b SettingsAssistant/pinning/tool-call). Pattern: builders strong at single-component correctness, weak at container assembly. Tests verify components in isolation; integration gaps caught only by code review.

Reconciliation tables are high-ROI (AA1, AB3, AD3, AD5, AE4, AD8b all used them; prevented 2-4h rework per workpackage). Make them required artifact in /architecture output. 15-30m investment up-front, prevents hours downstream.

Two-review-cycle pattern working well: Phase 4a NOT DONE, Phase 4b rework, Phase 4c DONE. Cost 2.5h (1h review + 1h fix + 0.5h re-review) is high but prevents post-ship defects. 100% blocker resolution rate (3/3 fixed, all accepted).

Architecture plan risks section (S10) identified 3 risks but missed integration wiring gaps. Risks are component-level; cross-component assembly gaps need explicit integration checklists. Would have added 4 checklist items to plan if anticipated.
